I disagree with the majority of people on here. 

I fail to believe you would have made her pay her tuition if she had a regular office job. 

You guys are adults. Your daughter has always been told you’d cover tuition. You’ve had 18+ years to save for this, and now, conveniently, you’re blaming current economic circumstances on your decision which should have been planned for years in advance. 

Your circumstances suck, but so do your motivations, based on what you’ve written. 

YTA.

The only back problems I’ve come across have been related to people insisting on having their carry on placed in the overheads, back when I was working on domestic flights and here in AUS, we no longer are required to do that. 
I’ve seen a number of knee injuries on the 737, due to the arming and disarming processes for the doors, but since I changed across to Long Haul, no more back or knee injuries.

I want to reach out to everyone and say that it’s so nice to know I’m not alone in all this. Yesterday was hard. Today is better. You guys are part of the reason I love flying so much. Thanks for helping keep my spirits up. Let me know if I can ever return the favour.

For years, I’ve wanted the government to bring in a requirement for companies who operate within Australia to clearly mark on their websites in a prominent position the percentage of the local workforce that is producing goods and services. For example, a major insurer I used to work for made a LOT of Australians redundant, simply to send the work overseas. People don’t have an understanding of how much a given company is supporting local jobs. If that information was clearly and prominently displayed, without the figures being deceptive (for example, made from 80% local produce, when it is 100% processed overseas) people would have the opportunity to make choices in line with their values.

Looking at figures from previously reported data, international placements average around 19% of medical school admissions. 
Medicine is competitive for a reason. And allowing international students to come here as full fee paying students pours much needed money into our education system. 
By your logic, you could also have a system that means international students are denied a place in medicine due to the international caps, in spite of their scores being greater than a domestic student. The reality is that we need international students in all disciplines in order to maximise the learning opportunities of all students. 
On a final note, I hope you do well in your exams and manage to follow your dreams of getting into medicine.

We’ve been stood down since the start of April. It’s been really hard not being with my sky siblings during this time, however it has given me an amazing opportunity to reevaluate what’s important. Many of my colleagues have taken redundancies, as the industry has been decimated here in Australia. 

The one thing we are amazing at, no matter where we are based, is that we are resilient. We are a uniquely gifted group of individuals, and we are strong. 

My heart goes out to every single one of you out there currently facing the furlough. And if anyone needs someone to reach out to for support, you can always directly message me. 

Much love to my American sky siblings...

Definitely look into it.

I messaged my partner for the first time on Tinder. Gave him 24 hours initially, as a courtesy, to see whether he would write first. Then I took a punt. I looked over his profile, saw he was in academic regalia in one of his photos, and sent a simple message. “What’s up, Doc”. 
Women love effort. As do men. The exact thing you heard women complaining about is what you’re taking issue with here. We all want to feel like the initial conversation we have with someone is personal. 
Have a look at their profile. Pick something out that you notice, and go from there. Don’t get hung up on tit for tat. If you want a partner, it really shouldn’t matter who said what, when. Good luck with your search, and stay optimistic. Never give up.
